question: Bind, 4v5, 26s left. Your team opens A. You lurk Hookah as Chamber (Rendezvous placed, Headhunter). Confirmed sound of a DEF rotating toward A through Hookah. What do you do?

options.label: Hold Hookah and punish the rotating DEF, covering the angle from your Rendezvous position with Headhunter
options.explication_courte: A confirmed rotation through your angle is the high-value lurk pick: you catch an isolated DEF mid-rotation, a free trade that turns the 4v5 into a 4v4.

options.label: Rotate quietly toward A Site to join your team's push now that the rotation is confirmed
options.explication_courte: Regrouping in a 4v5 is defensible to avoid isolation, but you abandon the rotation pick opportunity that was handed directly to you.

sources_option.citation: Regrouping to hit a site together is safer when down a player, but it forfeits the flank/rotation picks a lurker is positioned to punish.

options.label: Push toward B Site since it is draining of defenders to take the weakly held site
options.explication_courte: Solo-pushing B with 26s left is too slow: even if B empties, you cannot plant and defuse without team support in the remaining time.

sources_option.citation: Lurking is about information and picks, not solo-taking a site; a lone push into a site with an anchor and low time is a losing play.

options.label: Fire a Headhunter into the Hookah area to create noise and bait the DEF rotation early
options.explication_courte: Firing blind reveals your exact Hookah position, wastes Headhunter credits, and alerts the rotating DEF - you lose the ambush advantage entirely.

sources_option.citation: Be unpredictable and silent; making noise that reveals your lurk position hands the defenders exactly the information you were trying to deny them.

explication_longue:
Situation: Bind, 4v5 (one teammate down), 26 seconds left. Your team opens A. You lurk Hookah as Chamber with Rendezvous already placed (guaranteed fallback) and Headhunter. Confirmed sound of a DEF rotating from B toward A through Hookah.

This is the lurk's highest-value moment: a DEF rotating through your angle is isolated and moving - a free pick. Chamber's Rendezvous gives a guaranteed fallback after the shot: take the duel, eliminate the rotator, teleport to safety. This converts the 4v5 into a 4v4 right before your team pushes A.

Regrouping toward A (acceptable) is defensible if worried about isolation, but you abandon the best lurk opportunity the round offers. Pushing B solo (costly) is a timer problem: 26 seconds is not enough to solo-plant and defuse on B. Firing blind (mistake) reveals your position, wastes credits, and turns the ambush into a fair duel on the rotator's terms.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% hold Hookah and punish, ~22% rotate to A, ~15% push B (costly), ~6% fire blind (mistake).

sources.citation: Lurking nets valuable information, frags, and round wins by catching enemies off guard, especially rotating players focused elsewhere.
Patience and silence let you punish a confirmed rotation; the lurker hits the enemy when they are most vulnerable and in motion.
Cutting off or punishing a defensive rotation as it crosses the map is high-value; reading the rotation sound tells you where the pick is.

_gaps.incertitude: Punir la rotation (optimal) suppose que l'angle Hookah offre un tir net sur le chemin B-vers-A ; si la rotation passe hors ligne de vue, rotate-A (acceptable) monte en priorite. Ligne de vue exacte non encodee.
Le contexte du 4v5 (comment le 5e ATK est tombe) n'est pas precise ; il peut changer legerement le poids regrouper vs punir. Flagge honnetement.
Estimations depuis guides lurk/rotation (tracker, wecoach, sportskeeda) ; aucun dataset public sur la frequence punir-rotation vs regrouper en 4v5 par elo.
